metadata: Editorial biographies written from archived league evidence. Trade picks are audited measured direct-outcome candidates, not universal process grades. Waiver candidates are ranked from verified completed Sleeper adds/waivers matched to subsequent credited regular-season starts; source coverage remains incomplete before 2020 and for some roster-seat histories.

Stilly.biography: A 2016 founding manager, Stilly carried this franchise from its ESPN beginnings into the Sleeper era. The Portfolio Manager label is an editorial description of a trade-heavy franchise history, not a separately verified league-awarded nickname. Moves involving Mike Evans, Derrick Henry and Chase Brown form part of that story; Jayden Daniels later became a keeper investment. The defining tension of this franchise is constant reinvention: the moves do not always look tidy in isolation, but the trophy case proves at least one version came together when it mattered.
Stilly.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kirk Cousins (2021) currently leads at +55.20 above the positional starter benchmark.

JMid.biography: Blockbuster Rebuilder is an editorial description of JMid’s documented roster transactions, not an independently verified statement of intent. The 2024 season showed the upside: an 8–6 record and a documented league-high 1,730.22 points for. The trade-side archive includes Kyren Williams and Calvin Ridley in 2024, while James Cook is referenced elsewhere in the franchise history but is not confirmed as a trade asset by that dataset; Ja’Marr Chase and Joe Burrow appear in the credited starter archive. The Fellas record book still awaits JMid’s first championship, but the franchise has already demonstrated that its ceiling can match the league’s best.
JMid.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Rico Dowdle (2025) currently leads at +50.99 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tom.biography: Thommy is one of the four original 2016 managers. His three straight ESPN championships in 2016, 2017 and 2018 are the league’s first verified dynasty, followed by the 2024 championship. The original three-peat from 2016 through 2018 turned one successful season into a dynasty; the 2024 title proved that era was not the end of the story. Individual transaction metrics measure different outcomes from the four documented championship finishes and do not provide a complete evaluation of roster-building. Tee Higgins and Christian McCaffrey headline his recorded player contributions, but the defining figure is the manager behind four trophies. When the Fellas debate greatness, Tom starts with the simplest statistic: championships.
Tom.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Elijah Mitchell (2021) currently leads at +64.49 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stew.biography: A founding manager since 2016, Stew has been a constant opponent across every chapter of the league. The 2022 team went 11–3 and led in both points and potential points, showing how formidable a roster the constant dealing can produce. The verified trade-side archive includes Justin Jefferson and Ja’Marr Chase; references to Puka Nacua elsewhere in the franchise history should not be treated as independently verified trade acquisitions. One editorial reading of Stew’s record is the contrast between strong regular-season rosters and the documented championship results. He has assembled elite regular-season teams without yet turning that volume of moves into a documented championship.
Stew.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jamaal Williams (2022) currently leads at +61.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Scott.biography: Scott’s Fellas résumé is short in seasons but enormous in consequence. The 2025 championship arrived with a commanding documented title-game margin, putting a trophy on the shelf while longer-tenured managers were still chasing their first. The Converter is an editorial label for Scott’s documented results, not a verified account of how the nickname originated. Bijan Robinson anchors the recorded starter-production story, supported by productive contributions from James Cook and others. The unanswered question is not whether Scott can win a title—the 2025 season settled that—but how large the legacy can grow with more seasons.
Scott.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jauan Jennings (2024) currently leads at +42.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Mitch.biography: Mitch has made the regular season look almost like an engineering problem. The Math Problem is an editorial nickname for a franchise with high recorded regular-season scoring; it does not establish a particular lineup-building method. His 2025 team finished 13–1 and scored 1,894.88 points in the archived season summary, one of the clearest demonstrations of the method. The recorded starter archive features Deebo Samuel, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Josh Allen and Jonathan Taylor. Yet the résumé carries a conspicuous blank: no documented championship. That contrast between week-to-week dominance and postseason payoff is central to the Mitch story.
Mitch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Tyler Lockett (2022) currently leads at +96.22 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tony.biography: Tony’s 2021 championship is the cornerstone of a franchise built around calculated moves rather than constant noise. The Quiet Poker Player label is editorial shorthand; the archive separately documents trades, waivers, draft choices and credited lineup production. The trade-side archive documents Joe Mixon in 2021 and James Robinson in 2022; those are separate recorded trade years, and Zack Moss is not independently established as a trade acquisition by that dataset. Lamar Jackson, Jonathan Taylor and Stefon Diggs appear among the players who delivered in his starting lineup. Tony’s story is less about winning every argument and more about assembling one winning season.
Tony.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: James Robinson (2020) currently leads at +141.68 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stover.biography: Stover has been here since the eight-team 2016 season, when his PurpleHeaded YogurtSlingers name began the franchise that later became Gurt. The franchise’s history includes a 2022 championship and a strong 2024 regular season in the broader team archive. Stover’s Sleeper-era identity has now been reconciled across the continuous owner handle yogurtslinger15 and team-name aliases including YogurtSlingers, YogurtSlinger and Gurt. The current archive groups the documented 2020–2025 player, season and starter-value records under Stover rather than a generic historical roster seat.
Stover.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Philadelphia Eagles D/ST (2022) currently leads at +83.83 above the positional starter benchmark.

Kuhl.biography: Kuhl’s résumé is one of the Fellas’ most intriguing contradictions. The Process / Results Paradox is editorial framing. The trade-side archive documents J.K. Dobbins in 2024, but does not independently establish the acquisition method for Kyren Williams in 2023; the championship column has no documented title. Patrick Mahomes, Alvin Kamara and other productive starters populate the historical lineup ledger. Kuhl’s franchise invites a debate familiar to every fantasy player: when a manager makes good moves but does not get the corresponding final results, what deserves the credit and what deserves the blame?
Kuhl.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kyren Williams (2023) currently leads at +72.25 above the positional starter benchmark.

Birch.biography: Birch joined the league in 2017 as Hogan’s Heroes, reached the 2018 title game and won the championship in 2019 after an 11–2 regular season. The 2021 regular-season run of 11–2 added a different kind of evidence: this franchise can be consistent as well as daring. The historical archive contains notable positional trades and draft values, while Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson lead much of the credited lineup story. Trade and draft outcomes provide material for debate, but those outcomes alone cannot establish whether a decision was sound when it was made. The title remains the strongest answer to those arguments.
Birch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Aaron Rodgers (2020) currently leads at +90.05 above the positional starter benchmark.
